exercise_bank.title: Word Category Sort
exercise_bank.instructions: Here is a category: fruits. Say as many fruits as you can in one minute.

exercise_bank.title: Memory Chain
exercise_bank.instructions: Read these three items and remember them: apple, chair, drum. Look away, say them back in order, then add one more item of your own.

exercise_bank.title: Odd One Out
exercise_bank.instructions: Read these four words: apple, banana, carrot, orange. Say which one does not belong with the others and explain why.

exercise_bank.title: Follow the Steps
exercise_bank.instructions: Read these three steps: clap your hands, say your name, then touch your knee. Perform them out loud in that exact order.

exercise_bank.title: What Changed
exercise_bank.instructions: Look at three objects near you for ten seconds. Close your eyes and move one out of sight. Open your eyes and say which one is missing.

exercise_bank.title: Number Reverse
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this number sequence: 3, 9, 2, 7. Say the numbers back out loud in reverse order.

exercise_bank.title: Story Recall
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this short story: Maya packed a red umbrella before leaving for the park because the sky looked cloudy. Now say who the story is about, what she packed, and why.

exercise_bank.title: Sequence the Day
exercise_bank.instructions: Put these daily events in the correct order and say them out loud: eating breakfast, waking up, brushing teeth, going to school.

exercise_bank.title: Category Switch
exercise_bank.instructions: Name as many animals as you can for thirty seconds. Then switch and name as many fruits as you can for the next thirty seconds.

exercise_bank.title: Find the Rule
exercise_bank.instructions: Look at this number pattern: 2, 4, 6, 8. Say what number comes next and explain the rule you used.

exercise_bank.title: Two-Step Directions
exercise_bank.instructions: Touch your nose, then say your own name out loud, in that exact order.

exercise_bank.title: Word Association Chain
exercise_bank.instructions: Starting with the word ocean, say five words in a row where each new word connects to the one before it.

exercise_bank.title: Remember the List
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this grocery list: milk, bread, eggs, apples, cheese. Look away and say as many items as you can remember.

exercise_bank.title: Spot the Difference
exercise_bank.instructions: Read these two descriptions of a kitchen: Version 1 has a red kettle on the counter and two chairs at the table. Version 2 has a blue kettle on the counter and three chairs at the table. Say what is different between them.

exercise_bank.title: Mental Math Warmup
exercise_bank.instructions: Solve this in your head and say the answer out loud: what is seven plus five?

exercise_bank.title: Categorize and Explain
exercise_bank.instructions: Read these words: apple, car, banana, truck. Sort them into two groups and explain your reasoning out loud.

exercise_bank.title: Delayed Recall
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this fact: the capital of France is Paris. Say it out loud twice, then wait a moment and say it again from memory without looking back.

exercise_bank.title: Which Comes First
exercise_bank.instructions: Say which happens first and explain why: planting a seed, or watering a plant that has already grown.

exercise_bank.title: Attention to a Word
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this paragraph out loud: The cat sat on the mat. The dog ran past the cat. The bird watched from the tree. Then say how many times the word 'the' appears in it.

exercise_bank.title: Working Memory Sentence
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this sentence: The blue bicycle was leaning against the old wooden fence near the garden. Now, without looking back, say what color the bicycle was.

exercise_bank.title: Problem Solving Scenario
exercise_bank.instructions: Think out loud through this problem: what would you do if you lost your house key while no one else was home?

exercise_bank.title: Categorical Fluency
exercise_bank.instructions: Say as many things as you can that are red in one minute.

exercise_bank.title: Multi-Step Recipe Recall
exercise_bank.instructions: Read these steps: spread the peanut butter, add the jelly, then put the two slices of bread together. Say the steps back in order from memory.

exercise_bank.title: Visual Memory Snapshot
exercise_bank.instructions: Look closely at an object near you for five seconds. Close your eyes and describe it out loud from memory in as much detail as you can.

exercise_bank.title: Logical Sequencing
exercise_bank.instructions: Put these steps in the correct order and say them out loud: dry your hands, wash your hands, turn off the tap.

exercise_bank.title: Item Pairing Recall
exercise_bank.instructions: Say three pairs of related items, such as sock and shoe, and explain out loud why each pair goes together.

exercise_bank.title: Focus While Distracted
exercise_bank.instructions: Say the days of the week in order out loud while tapping your hand on a surface the whole time without losing your place.

exercise_bank.title: Time Orientation Check
exercise_bank.instructions: Say today's day of the week, the month, and roughly what time of day it is right now.

exercise_bank.title: Cause and Effect
exercise_bank.instructions: Say out loud what would happen if you left a bowl of ice cream out in the sun.

exercise_bank.title: Number Sequence Recall
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this sequence: 5, 1, 8, 3, 6. Say the numbers back out loud in the exact same order.

exercise_bank.title: Planning a Task
exercise_bank.instructions: Describe out loud, step by step, how you would plan a simple birthday party.

exercise_bank.title: Word Definition Retrieval
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this word: generous. Say its definition out loud without using the word itself.

exercise_bank.title: Shifting Attention Task
exercise_bank.instructions: For thirty seconds, name objects near you by their color. Then for the next thirty seconds, name the same objects by their shape instead.

exercise_bank.title: Prospective Memory Prompt
exercise_bank.instructions: Remember to say the word banana out loud at the very end of your next response, after everything else you say.

exercise_bank.title: Estimating Quantities
exercise_bank.instructions: Look around and pick a group of similar objects nearby, like books or pens. Estimate how many there are, then count them and say out loud whether your guess was close.

exercise_bank.title: Following Complex Directions
exercise_bank.instructions: Read these four steps in order: stand up, say your favorite color, sit back down, then clap once. Perform all four steps out loud.

exercise_bank.title: Inference Practice
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this scenario: Sam walked in soaking wet and holding a dripping umbrella. Say what you think most likely happened outside, and explain your reasoning.

exercise_bank.title: Simon Says Listening
exercise_bank.instructions: Read these instructions, but only perform the ones that start with 'Simon says': 1) Simon says touch your ear. 2) Clap your hands. 3) Simon says say your name out loud. Say out loud which actions you performed.

exercise_bank.title: Recall the Reason
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this short story: Leo gave his umbrella to a stranger even though it started to rain on his walk home. Say why you think Leo made that choice.

exercise_bank.title: Verbal Fluency Letter Game
exercise_bank.instructions: Say as many words as you can that start with the letter S in one minute.

exercise_bank.title: Mental Flexibility Sorting
exercise_bank.instructions: Name five objects near you. Sort them into groups by color and say the groups out loud, then re-sort the same objects by size and say the new groups.

exercise_bank.title: Short Term Recall Numbers
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this number sequence: 4, 8, 1, 6. Say the numbers back out loud immediately in the same order.

exercise_bank.title: Planning Ahead Task
exercise_bank.instructions: Describe out loud what you would need to pack for an overnight trip, and in what order you would pack it.

exercise_bank.title: Attention to Detail Reading
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this paragraph out loud: The green car parked next to the red house had one flat tire. Then say one detail from the paragraph that stood out to you.

exercise_bank.title: Comparing Two Items
exercise_bank.instructions: Compare a bicycle and a car out loud, naming two ways they are similar and two ways they are different.

exercise_bank.title: Task Switching Drill
exercise_bank.instructions: Count up by twos out loud from zero to twenty, then immediately count down by threes out loud from thirty.

exercise_bank.title: Everyday Problem Solving
exercise_bank.instructions: Say out loud what you would do if you were at a store and could not find an item you needed.

exercise_bank.title: Reasoning Riddle
exercise_bank.instructions: Solve this riddle out loud: I have keys but no locks, I have space but no room. What am I?

exercise_bank.title: Memory for Names
exercise_bank.instructions: Read these three names: Priya, Marcus, and Elena. Look away and say all three names back from memory.

exercise_bank.title: Organizing Information
exercise_bank.instructions: Read these words: dog, spoon, cat, fork, hamster, plate. Group them into logical categories out loud and explain your groupings.

exercise_bank.title: Balloon Breaths
exercise_bank.instructions: Take a slow deep breath in like blowing up a balloon, then say 'I can speak slowly and clearly' as you let it out evenly.

exercise_bank.title: Bounce the Ball Syllables
exercise_bank.instructions: Say each syllable out loud like you are bouncing a ball: wa-ter-mel-on, but-ter-fly, el-e-phant.

exercise_bank.title: Slow Motion Reader
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this sentence out loud like a robot in slow motion: The. Big. Dog. Ran. Fast. Then say it again at a normal, clear pace.

exercise_bank.title: Dragon Breaths
exercise_bank.instructions: Take a big breath in like a dragon about to breathe fire, then say 'I am a strong speaker' slowly as you let it out.

exercise_bank.title: Pre-Talk Breath Reset
exercise_bank.instructions: Breathe in for three seconds and out for four, then say your name and one fact about yourself out loud.

exercise_bank.title: No Filler Recap
exercise_bank.instructions: Say out loud what you did yesterday without using um, uh, or like. Pause silently instead whenever you need a moment.

exercise_bank.title: Easy Onset Practice
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these sentences starting with a gentle stretched first sound instead of a hard stop: Hhhello, how are you. Iiit was a good day.

exercise_bank.title: Comma Breathing
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this paragraph out loud, taking a visible pause and breath at every comma: The morning sun rose slowly, the birds began to sing, and the town woke up quietly.

exercise_bank.title: Metronome Reading
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this sentence out loud, placing equal timing on each word like a steady beat: I walk to the store every single day.

exercise_bank.title: Unscripted Topic Talk
exercise_bank.instructions: Talk out loud for ninety seconds about your morning routine, focusing on staying calm and paced.

exercise_bank.title: Ship or Sheep
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these word pairs out loud, making each one sound clearly distinct: ship - sheep, chip - cheap, sip - seep.

exercise_bank.title: Snake Sounds
exercise_bank.instructions: Make a long ssssss sound out loud for five seconds, then say sun, sand, snake, soup.

exercise_bank.title: Red Rabbit Run
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this three times out loud: Red rabbit runs around. Say it a little faster each time while staying clear.

exercise_bank.title: Thumbs Up Thursday
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these words out loud, placing your tongue gently between your teeth for the th sound: thumb, think, three, Thursday.

exercise_bank.title: Lion or Line
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these pairs out loud, listening for the L sound at the start: lion - line, light - night, low - flow.

exercise_bank.title: Silly Sally
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this three times out loud: Silly Sally sells seashells. Start slow, then speed up carefully.

exercise_bank.title: Sound Story
exercise_bank.instructions: Tell a short story out loud using as many S words as you can, such as sun, snake, sandwich, and swim.

exercise_bank.title: Funny Fox
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these words out loud, feeling your top teeth touch your bottom lip: fox, fun, fish, five, village, voice.

exercise_bank.title: Think or Sink
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these pairs out loud: think - sink, three - free, thank - sank.

exercise_bank.title: Really Clearly
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this three times out loud at increasing speed: Really red lorries rolled down really long roads.

exercise_bank.title: Text to Talk
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this out loud as clearly as you would type it: I am on my way, be there in five minutes.

exercise_bank.title: Sentence Final S
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these sentences out loud, emphasizing the final S sound: The cats chase the rats. She wears dresses to classes.

exercise_bank.title: Very or Wary
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these pairs out loud: very - wary, vine - wine, vest - west.

exercise_bank.title: Six Slippery Snails
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this three times out loud: Six slippery snails slid slowly seaward. Go slow, then speed up carefully.

exercise_bank.title: R vs L Pair Drill
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these word pairs out loud: right - light, road - load, rip - lip, correct - collect.

exercise_bank.title: Thirty Three Thieves
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this three times out loud at increasing speed: Thirty-three thieves thought they thrilled the throne throughout Thursday.

exercise_bank.title: Peter Piper Advanced
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this three times out loud at increasing speed, keeping every P crisp: Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers.

exercise_bank.title: F and V Contrast
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these pairs out loud, feeling your top teeth on your bottom lip: fan - van, feel - veal, fast - vast, fine - vine.

exercise_bank.title: Stress Shift Challenge
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these word pairs out loud, noticing the stress shift: RE-cord vs re-CORD, PRE-sent vs pre-SENT.

exercise_bank.title: Natural Linking
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these phrases out loud as one smooth connected sound: turn it off, kind of, I don't know.

exercise_bank.title: Cluster Practice
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these consonant clusters out loud slowly: str in street, spl in splash, thr in three, str in strong.

exercise_bank.title: Emphasis Changes Meaning
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this sentence out loud four times, stressing a different word each time: I never said she took it.

exercise_bank.title: Clear and Quick
exercise_bank.instructions: Describe your weekend plans out loud in under thirty seconds, keeping every word fully clear.

exercise_bank.title: Sentence-Per-Breath
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this sentence out loud, then pause and take a new breath: I am learning to speak smoothly. Now say the next sentence on a new breath: I feel calm and clear.

exercise_bank.title: Paced Paragraph Reading
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this paragraph out loud at a deliberately slow, even pace: The morning sun rose slowly over the quiet city. People began their day, walking calmly to work.

exercise_bank.title: Diaphragmatic Breathing Drill
exercise_bank.instructions: Inhale deeply through your nose for four seconds, hold for two, then say this full sentence as you exhale over six seconds: I can speak with a calm, steady voice.

exercise_bank.title: Filler-Free Minute
exercise_bank.instructions: Speak out loud for one minute about your day without using filler words, pausing silently instead when needed.

exercise_bank.title: Pause at Punctuation
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this paragraph out loud, pausing visibly at every comma and full stop: Last weekend, I went to the mall with my friends. We had lunch, watched a movie, and walked around for hours.

exercise_bank.title: Clap and Talk
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this sentence out loud, clapping once on every word: I like to play outside. Then say it again a little slower.

exercise_bank.title: Question Ping Pong
exercise_bank.instructions: Take a breath, then answer this question slowly and out loud: What is your favourite colour?

exercise_bank.title: Vowel Zoo
exercise_bank.instructions: Say each vowel sound out loud with its animal cue: A as in cat, E as in elephant, I as in iguana, O as in octopus, U as in umbrella.

exercise_bank.title: Smooth Talker
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this phrase out loud as one smooth flow without stopping between words: I want to go to the park.

exercise_bank.title: Question or Statement
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this sentence out loud as a statement, then as a question: You like ice cream. Notice how your voice rises for the question.

exercise_bank.title: Vowel Contrast Drill
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these pairs out loud: ship - sheep, bit - beat, full - fool, bed - bad.

exercise_bank.title: Photograph Stress Drill
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these words out loud, placing stress on the correct syllable: PHO-to-graph, pho-TOG-ra-pher, pho-to-GRAPH-ic.

exercise_bank.title: Baseline Clarity Passage
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this passage out loud at a natural pace: Yesterday I walked to the store and bought some fresh bread and vegetables.

exercise_bank.title: Group Intro Practice
exercise_bank.instructions: Say out loud an introduction of yourself to an imaginary group, including your name and one hobby.

exercise_bank.title: Read With Feeling
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this sentence out loud with natural rise and fall in your voice: I honestly cannot believe that happened. That is the most surprising thing I have heard all week.

exercise_bank.title: Slow Read Relay
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this sentence out loud at half your normal speed: Yesterday I went to school and had a really interesting class about history. Then say it again at normal speed, keeping the same clarity.

exercise_bank.title: Animal Race
exercise_bank.instructions: Say each animal name out loud slowly, one syllable at a time, like walking it across the room: Tor-toise. Tur-key. Pen-guin. Cro-co-dile.

exercise_bank.title: Synonym Swap
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this word: happy. Say a synonym out loud, a word that means almost the same thing.

exercise_bank.title: Antonym Match
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this word: hot. Say its opposite out loud.

exercise_bank.title: Describe the Object
exercise_bank.instructions: Pick an object near you and describe it out loud using at least four different adjectives.

exercise_bank.title: Build a Sentence
exercise_bank.instructions: Read these three words: dog, umbrella, quickly. Use all three in one grammatically correct sentence out loud.

exercise_bank.title: Fix the Sentence
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this sentence: She go to the store yesterday. Say the corrected version out loud.

exercise_bank.title: Past, Present, Future
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this verb: run. Say it out loud in the past, present, and future tense.

exercise_bank.title: Compare Two Things
exercise_bank.instructions: Compare a chair and a box out loud using comparative language, such as 'The chair is bigger than the box.'

exercise_bank.title: Category Naming
exercise_bank.instructions: Name five items out loud that belong in this category: kitchen tools.

exercise_bank.title: Retell the Story
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this short story: Maya packed a red umbrella before leaving for the park because the sky looked cloudy. Retell it out loud in your own words using complete sentences.

exercise_bank.title: Ask a Question
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this statement: The movie starts at seven. Turn it into a question out loud that could get that statement as an answer.

exercise_bank.title: Sequencing Words
exercise_bank.instructions: Describe out loud how to make a sandwich, using sequencing words like first, next, then, and finally.

exercise_bank.title: Idiom Meaning
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this idiom: it's raining cats and dogs. Explain out loud what it really means.

exercise_bank.title: Plural Practice
exercise_bank.instructions: Read these singular nouns: child, mouse, cat. Say the correct plural form of each one out loud.

exercise_bank.title: Describe a Process
exercise_bank.instructions: Explain out loud, step by step, how you would tie your shoes.

exercise_bank.title: Compound Sentences
exercise_bank.instructions: Read these two short sentences: I was hungry. I made a sandwich. Combine them into one longer sentence out loud using and, but, or because.

exercise_bank.title: Vocabulary Expansion
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this simple word: big. Say a more advanced or specific word out loud that means something similar.

exercise_bank.title: Answer Wh Questions
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this passage: On Saturday, Ben rode his bike to the lake and watched the sunset with his sister. Say out loud who, what, when, and where.

exercise_bank.title: Story Prediction
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this story opening: The old wooden door creaked open, revealing a room no one had entered in years. Say out loud what you think will happen next.

exercise_bank.title: Pronoun Practice
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this sentence: Sarah gave the book to Sarah's brother. Say the sentence out loud replacing the second 'Sarah' with the correct pronoun.

exercise_bank.title: Explain a Word
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this word: umbrella. Explain its meaning out loud without saying the word itself.

exercise_bank.title: Descriptive Storytelling
exercise_bank.instructions: Describe a place you love out loud using as much descriptive detail as you can.

exercise_bank.title: Cause and Effect Sentences
exercise_bank.instructions: Read these two ideas: It started raining. We went inside. Combine them into one cause and effect sentence out loud using because or so.

exercise_bank.title: Following a Recipe Aloud
exercise_bank.instructions: Read these steps: toast the bread, spread the butter, add the jam. Say the steps back out loud using sequencing language like first, next, and then.

exercise_bank.title: Multiple Meaning Words
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this word: bat. Say two different meanings of this word out loud.

exercise_bank.title: Making Comparisons
exercise_bank.instructions: Read these three sizes: small, medium, large. Use comparative and superlative forms to compare them out loud, such as small, smaller, smallest.

exercise_bank.title: Story Sequencing
exercise_bank.instructions: Read these three events out of order: she ate breakfast, she woke up, she brushed her teeth. Say them out loud in the correct logical order.

exercise_bank.title: Conversation Starters
exercise_bank.instructions: Say out loud how you would start a conversation with someone new, including a greeting and a question.

exercise_bank.title: Categorization and Explanation
exercise_bank.instructions: Read these words: apple, hammer, banana, wrench. Sort them into categories out loud and explain your reasoning.

exercise_bank.title: Figurative Language Spotting
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this sentence: Her smile was as bright as the sun. Say out loud whether it is a simile, a metaphor, or literal language, and explain why.

exercise_bank.title: Expressing Opinions
exercise_bank.instructions: Say your opinion out loud on this topic and explain one reason why: should students have homework on weekends?

exercise_bank.title: Verb Tense Correction
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this sentence: Yesterday I go to the park. Say the corrected version out loud.

exercise_bank.title: Descriptive Question Game
exercise_bank.instructions: Think of an object in your mind and give three descriptive clues about it out loud, without naming it.

exercise_bank.title: Summarizing a Passage
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this passage: The team practiced every day for a month before the big game. On game day, they played their best and won by two points. Summarize it out loud in two or three sentences.

exercise_bank.title: Using Prepositions
exercise_bank.instructions: Describe out loud where an object near you is located, using a preposition like on, under, next to, or between.

exercise_bank.title: Making Requests Politely
exercise_bank.instructions: Say out loud a polite way to ask for something, such as 'Could I please have...'

exercise_bank.title: Story Elements
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this short story: Jamie found a lost puppy in the park and could not find its owner anywhere. Say out loud the character, the setting, and the problem.

exercise_bank.title: Word Categorization Speed
exercise_bank.instructions: Read these words: rock, tree, chair, flower, table, bird. Sort them out loud into two categories, such as living and non-living.

exercise_bank.title: Conjunction Practice
exercise_bank.instructions: Read these two sentences: I wanted to go outside. It was raining. Combine them out loud using a conjunction such as although, since, or unless.

exercise_bank.title: Explaining a Rule
exercise_bank.instructions: Explain out loud, step by step, the rules of a simple game you know to someone who has never played it.

exercise_bank.title: Descriptive Comparisons
exercise_bank.instructions: Describe out loud the difference between a cat and a tiger.

exercise_bank.title: Sentence Expansion
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this short sentence: The dog ran. Say an expanded version of it out loud with more descriptive detail.

exercise_bank.title: Listening for Details
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this passage: The blue car stopped outside the tall red brick building at exactly noon. Say out loud three specific details you noticed.

exercise_bank.title: Making Predictions From Titles
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this story title: The Day the Lights Went Out. Say out loud what you think the story might be about.

exercise_bank.title: Using Because and So
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this scenario: the ground was wet. Explain out loud why it might have happened using because, and what likely happened as a result using so.

exercise_bank.title: Real-Life Directions
exercise_bank.instructions: Give directions out loud from your front door to your kitchen, using clear sequential language.

exercise_bank.title: Explaining Feelings
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this scenario: a character just won first place in a competition. Describe out loud how they might be feeling and why.

exercise_bank.title: Word Retrieval Warmup
exercise_bank.instructions: Say out loud the first word that comes to mind for each of these categories: an animal, a color, a food.

exercise_bank.title: Building Descriptions with Senses
exercise_bank.instructions: Describe an object near you out loud using how it looks, feels, sounds, and smells.

exercise_bank.title: Correcting Word Order
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this scrambled sentence: park the to went dog the. Say the words out loud in the correct order.

exercise_bank.title: Two Truths and Explanation
exercise_bank.instructions: Say two true facts about yourself out loud and explain each one using complete, detailed sentences.

exercise_bank.title: Show and Tell
exercise_bank.instructions: Pick your favourite object nearby and say three things about it out loud. Take your time, there is no rush.

exercise_bank.title: Picture Detective
exercise_bank.instructions: Look around you and describe everything you can see out loud, like a detective finding clues.

exercise_bank.title: Pretend Phone Call
exercise_bank.instructions: Pretend you are calling a friend to invite them to your birthday party. Say out loud what you would tell them.

exercise_bank.title: Quick Questions
exercise_bank.instructions: Answer these out loud in full sentences: What is your favourite food? What do you like to do after school?

exercise_bank.title: My Best Day Ever
exercise_bank.instructions: Tell a story out loud about the best day you ever had. Try to talk for at least one minute.

exercise_bank.title: Order at a Restaurant
exercise_bank.instructions: Pretend you are ordering your favourite food at a restaurant. Say out loud what you would tell the waiter.

exercise_bank.title: Make Up a Story
exercise_bank.instructions: Make up a story out loud about a superhero: who they are, what their power is, and what happened to them today.

exercise_bank.title: Favourite Things
exercise_bank.instructions: Answer out loud in full sentences: What is your favourite movie and why? What are you really good at?

exercise_bank.title: Describe Your Space
exercise_bank.instructions: Look around your room and describe out loud what you see for thirty seconds, no script needed.

exercise_bank.title: Talking to a Teacher
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice out loud asking a teacher to explain something: 'Excuse me, I had a question about the homework.'

exercise_bank.title: Hot Seat Questions
exercise_bank.instructions: Answer out loud, confidently: What are you proud of this year? What do you wish more people knew about you?

exercise_bank.title: Tell Me About Something You Love
exercise_bank.instructions: Talk out loud for sixty seconds about a game, show, or hobby you love, as if recommending it to a friend.

exercise_bank.title: Class Presentation Practice
exercise_bank.instructions: Deliver out loud the opening thirty seconds of an imaginary school presentation on any topic you choose.

exercise_bank.title: Small Talk Warmup
exercise_bank.instructions: Answer these out loud naturally: How was your weekend? What have you been up to lately?

exercise_bank.title: Unprepared Opinion
exercise_bank.instructions: Give your honest opinion out loud for sixty seconds without preparing: should school start later in the morning?

exercise_bank.title: Saying No Confidently
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice out loud saying no politely but clearly, as if a friend asked you to do something you did not want to do.

exercise_bank.title: Describe What You See
exercise_bank.instructions: Describe a photo or scene around you out loud for thirty seconds without overthinking your wording.

exercise_bank.title: Mock Interview Question
exercise_bank.instructions: Answer out loud as if in a job interview: Tell me about yourself. Aim for sixty to ninety seconds.

exercise_bank.title: Asking for Something
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice out loud asking a coworker for help with a task, speaking clearly without over-apologizing.

exercise_bank.title: Unprepared Topic Talk
exercise_bank.instructions: Speak out loud for two minutes about a skill you would like to learn, without preparing in advance.

exercise_bank.title: Small Talk Starters
exercise_bank.instructions: Answer these out loud naturally: How was your weekend? and What do you do for work?

exercise_bank.title: 30 Second Pitch
exercise_bank.instructions: Say out loud a brief, confident introduction of yourself as if meeting a room of new colleagues.

exercise_bank.title: Difficult Question Practice
exercise_bank.instructions: Take a breath, then answer this out loud directly and confidently: What is your greatest weakness?

exercise_bank.title: Tell Me Something Good
exercise_bank.instructions: Tell out loud about something positive that happened to you recently, taking your time.

exercise_bank.title: Compliment Practice
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice giving a genuine compliment out loud, as if the person were standing in front of you.

exercise_bank.title: Sharing an Opinion Respectfully
exercise_bank.instructions: Share an opinion out loud on this topic while acknowledging someone might disagree: is it better to read the book or watch the movie first?

exercise_bank.title: Introducing a Friend
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice out loud introducing a friend to someone new, saying their name and one nice thing about them.

exercise_bank.title: Standing Up for Yourself
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice out loud a calm, clear response to someone interrupting you mid-conversation.

exercise_bank.title: Asking for Directions
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice out loud confidently asking a stranger for directions to a nearby place.

exercise_bank.title: Ordering Confidently
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice out loud placing a food order clearly and confidently without rushing or mumbling.

exercise_bank.title: Speaking Up in a Group
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice out loud sharing an idea, as if speaking up in a group meeting or class discussion.

exercise_bank.title: Handling a Compliment
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice out loud responding graciously to this compliment: 'You did such a great job on that.'

exercise_bank.title: Apologizing Clearly
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice out loud a short, sincere apology for showing up late to meet a friend.

exercise_bank.title: Sharing Good News
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice out loud telling a friend some good news with enthusiasm in your voice.

exercise_bank.title: Disagreeing Politely
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice out loud politely disagreeing with this opinion: 'I think pizza is the best food ever.'

exercise_bank.title: Answering Unexpectedly
exercise_bank.instructions: Answer this out loud right now, without any time to think first: What is one thing that made you smile this week?

exercise_bank.title: Recounting an Achievement
exercise_bank.instructions: Talk out loud for thirty seconds about something you accomplished that you are proud of.

exercise_bank.title: Speaking to a Stranger
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice out loud a short, friendly exchange you might have with someone you just met.

exercise_bank.title: Presenting an Idea
exercise_bank.instructions: Pitch a simple idea out loud, like a weekend plan, as if trying to convince a friend to agree.

exercise_bank.title: Confident Body and Voice
exercise_bank.instructions: Say a short introduction out loud, focusing on a steady, clear, and confident tone of voice.

exercise_bank.title: Handling Interruptions
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice out loud calmly finishing your thought after being interrupted mid-sentence.

exercise_bank.title: Toast or Congratulations
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice out loud giving a short congratulatory message to a friend who just achieved something.

exercise_bank.title: Answering Under Pressure
exercise_bank.instructions: Take a breath, then answer this out loud calmly: What would you do if your plans suddenly changed?

exercise_bank.title: Group Introduction
exercise_bank.instructions: Introduce yourself out loud to an imaginary new group, stating your name and one interest.

exercise_bank.title: Explaining a Mistake
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice out loud calmly explaining a small mistake you made and what you learned from it.

exercise_bank.title: Requesting Feedback
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice out loud asking someone for honest feedback on something you did.

exercise_bank.title: Voicing a Boundary
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice out loud calmly stating a personal boundary in a respectful but firm way.

exercise_bank.title: Celebrating Someone Else
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice out loud speaking warmly about a friend's or family member's recent success.

exercise_bank.title: Starting a Difficult Conversation
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice out loud the opening line of a conversation you have been putting off.

exercise_bank.title: Ending on a High Note
exercise_bank.instructions: Practice out loud a warm, confident goodbye at the end of a conversation or meeting.
